comments.text: Travel nurse since 2016 here. It surprises me not at all that this push started in NC, although any southeastern state would have been as likely. I've worked all over the country, and in general the hospitals in the southeastern states are the most financially stressed, pay the least, and have the most unsafe working conditions. There's outliers of course, but in general that's how it is.  There's also been a general move everywhere toward leaning into hiring travel nurses instead of paying permanent nursing staff better. Even though that theoretically gives me more options, its a bad thing for nursing overall and I'd rather see nursing be better than have more opportunities personally. Moves toward bidding increase disparities in access to health care, especially in southeastern and central midwestern states.

comments.text: This is EXACTLY what happened in my profession, medical transcription.  First it was voice recognition software that cut the workforce by 50%.  We still had to edit the awful speech "products" which are horrible to this day btw. And our pay as experienced, educated, medical language specialists was lowered from 15-23 cpl down to 4 cpl for editing. Medical knowledge, accuracy, and quality didn't matter anymore - it was more important to save a few bucks...until the PTB discovered that VR wasn't as great as they thought it would be - they needed a thinking human after all (examples being medication dosages, 15 mg and 50 mg sound very similar, rights and lefts were dictated wrong, etc.) so their brilliant idea was to now offer employment positions as "scribes", basically doing the same exact work but at 50% LESS pay. And let me tell you, there were people who worked for that abysmal pay.  Medical transcriptionists previously made excellent pay, had to maintain a 99% accuracy rate and baseline 150 lines per hour. Now?  The absolute garbage I saw in reports was astounding.  We would have been fired for the mistakes I saw in the patient reports - people could have died (and probably did) by not having knowledgeable experienced transcriptionists at the other end spotting discrepancies, physician errors, inconsistencies, etc.  I became so disgusted with it all that I retired early.  Ultimately, when standards are lowered, it is the patients that are affected.

comments.author: @MichaelGroff-zh3fm
comments.text: I work in mid level management at a hospital. No one in this video knows what they are discussing. Lets discuss critical staffing model and what that is. Critical staffing is a method were there is a need to filling essential roles fast during high demand periods emergencies, and staff shortages. Its a shift and nothing more. These are commonly referred as bid shifts by staff. They offer normally time and a half wage (1.5x your hourly rate). Now nurses saw a salary increase of about $30k to $40K in salary due to the pandemic rate hikes a crossed the nation. Putting about 2.5 to 3 million in increased salary burden on say a facility with 500 staffed beds annually. Critical staffing model is not part of regular daily operational staffing, again only affects a gap in shift demand. So rather than asking for volunteers for bid shift pay traditionally 1.5x hourly rate the hospital in question is going to let nurses bid for the shift and the lowest bidder wins which resolves infighting with nurses and favoritism which is a thing with bid shift because the rate is better. This also benefits the hospital and it allows a decrease in salary burden on the books at the end of the fiscal year and is a soft savings for a facility that is probably financially stressed.
